objective: A frozen exploratory census, exact: square, triangular and honeycomb n x n tori for n = 6, 8, 10, 12 and 16, re-routed at random sets built from the torus or from its line network by 4 n^2 random face-boundary toggles kept when the result is a network, four seeds each; read persistence, flips, non-degeneracy, the plain first need, single fastest ways and ring-graph balls, testing that random re-routings keep every contact persistent with no flip, that none reads its distance plainly, and that small rings are late.
status: Closed: refuted 2026-11-09 (exploratory, exact; frozen contract pre-registered in 8291ad565): of 120 re-routed square, triangular and honeycomb tori (n = 6 to 16), the 60 random re-routings from the torus keep every contact persistent with no flip at any contact (non-degenerate, genus 15 to 189) and are all late, but H1 and H2 fail on the 60 line-start networks, where no face toggle could be kept: they are the line networks, with a flip at every contact and on time. H3 holds: on tori of n >= 12 every ring of at most 12 contacts is late for some target (4,006 of 4,006).
title: Re-routed lattice tori: a census
